bull.b: Early revenue growth indicates that ZEVASKYN is beginning to convert clinical adoption into commercial sales. If patient treatment volumes continue rising, this expanding revenue base could improve operating leverage and strengthen Abeona’s position in the rare-disease therapy market over the coming quarters.

A broader qualified treatment-center network improves patient access and creates a more scalable commercial infrastructure for ZEVASKYN. Greater geographic coverage can support sustained treatment growth, deepen physician familiarity, and reduce reliance on a small number of launch sites as activation progresses.

The NTAP decision provides a meaningful reimbursement pathway for eligible hospital use and externally validates the therapy’s clinical improvement. Supplemental payment support may reduce adoption friction with providers and improve the durability of commercial access as Medicare-linked demand develops.

bear.b: Abeona remains dependent on external financing or materially improved operations because substantial cash burn continues alongside deep net losses. This weak internal cash generation can constrain investment choices, increase funding dependence, and pressure financial flexibility while the commercial business scales.

Manufacturing failures can eliminate revenue even when patients are treated, directly weakening unit economics and making quarterly sales less predictable. The related assay-specification review adds regulatory uncertainty, while recurring process variability could delay the reliable scaling needed for durable profitability.

ZEVASKYN’s narrow shelf life and variable site-to-treatment timing make commercialization operationally complex. Scheduling disruptions or delayed center ramp-up can leave treatment capacity unused, slow patient conversion, and create uneven revenue growth even as the treatment-center footprint expands.
